title: Sebastian and the Ghost
premise: Silas Nakamura interprets for a doomed peace delegation, but when a diplomatic flight vanishes from every record while still airborne, she realizes the erasure is a cover for a massacre her own government sanctioned. Hunting the truth through shifting border checkpoints and rewritten rules, she discovers her late father's hidden role in the original crime—and that the 'ghost' everyone fears is a survivor who holds the evidence. To survive the checkpoint shift change, Silas must publicly surrender the secret she's protected all her life: her own erased identity, traded for justice the law will never deliver.
about_author: Bram Ashgrove is the pen name of a former conflict-zone translator who now writes thrillers about the people who speak between nations. He lives near a border he refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Language of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Silas Nakamura, interpreter for a fragile peace delegation, softens a general's threat into a promise and watches the room relax. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the quiet shame of a woman whose job is making violence sound polite.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: The delegation's liaison flight to Meridian fails to arrive; every manifest, radar log, and passenger list has been scrubbed within the hour. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cold vertigo as she realizes reality itself has been edited.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Silas files a discrepancy report and finds her own report already answered—denied, dated, signed with her name. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the horror of being framed inside the machine she trusted.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't on the Plane
chapters.summary: A delegation aide, Tomas Vey, quietly asks Silas to mistranslate a question about the flight. She refuses; he vanishes from the hotel registry by morning. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Nine
chapters.summary: Silas crosses a border checkpoint and notices the shift-change ledger lists a passenger 'transferred' the night the flight vanished. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the first thread of a pattern.

chapters.title: What My Father Buried
chapters.summary: Searching her dead father's effects, Silas finds a diplomatic pouch key and a photo of him with the general whose words she softened in chapter one. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: inheritance as betrayal.

chapters.title: The Ghost Speaks
chapters.summary: An anonymous call in a dialect only three interpreters know reaches Silas: a survivor of the flight is alive and hiding. POV: Silas, with a brief intercut of the caller's hands counting pills. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as danger.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback: how Silas erased her family name after a tribunal scandal, becoming 'Nakamura' by paperwork alone. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the cost of the invisibility she thought was safety.

chapters.title: The General's Interpreter
chapters.summary: Silas is reassigned to the general himself, who tests her loyalty with a phrase only the flight's crew would know. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: playing a role while her cover thins.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Shift Change
chapters.summary: Silas steals a copy of the checkpoint ledger and finds her father's signature authorizing the 'transfer'—dated after his recorded death. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Safehouse in the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Guided by the caller, Silas reaches the survivor: a young flight engineer, Ada, burned and half-starved, carrying a data drive. POV: alternating Silas and Ada. Emotional beat: two erased women recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Drive Holds
chapters.summary: The drive contains the flight's real manifest—including Silas's father, alive, and a second passenger: the general's son. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the secret worth killing for, finally named.

chapters.title: The Delegation Collapses
chapters.summary: Peace talks fail spectacularly; the general blames 'terrorist interference' and checkpoints lock down. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the trap closing as the window narrows.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Archive
chapters.summary: Silas breaks into the national records annex to verify her father's death date and finds her own file—her original name flagged for 'termination on contact.' POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the past hunting her in the present.

chapters.title: Tomas, Alive and Bought
chapters.summary: Tomas Vey reappears, working for the other side, and offers Silas immunity if she surrenders the drive. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Ada reveals the general's son ordered the flight down to fake his own death and escape a corruption tribunal. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: rage finding its true target.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Safehouse
chapters.summary: The safehouse is raided; Silas escapes with the drive but Ada is taken, and Silas realizes her caller sold them out to save his own family. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the loneliest chapter—trust spent, nothing returned.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Shift Change
chapters.summary: Silas has until the midnight shift change to cross with the drive before the ledger—and Ada—are erased. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: a countdown with her whole life inside it.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: At the checkpoint, Silas confronts the general's son and trades the one secret worth killing for: she broadcasts the drive's manifest over the delegation's open channel, naming everyone—including herself under her true name. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the climax—identity as a weapon.

chapters.title: Ada, Returned
chapters.summary: Exposed, the general's faction fractures; soldiers loyal to the tribunal free Ada from the checkpoint holding room. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: rescue that costs the rescuers everything.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: The general falls not to a court but to public record; the son flees; the tribunal that once erased Silas quietly dissolves. No one is formally charged. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: bitter, honest victory.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Ghost
chapters.summary: Silas, living openly under her real name, meets Ada at a border café; Ada asks who 'Sebastian' was—the name in her father's pouch. Silas smiles: it was the alias her father used to survive, and now the name she chooses. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed, identity finally her own.
